# Disagreement Log — Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 15

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 24

---

## Disagreements

**v. 1** — "kind and true" (EMET) vs. "gracious and true" (LOGOS) vs. "kind and faithful" (PNEUMA). Greek χρηστὸς καὶ ἀληθής. χρηστός = useful, good, kind, gracious. LOGOS's "gracious" preferred as slightly more elevated.

**v. 1** — "governing all things in mercy" (EMET) vs. "ordering all things in mercy" (LOGOS) vs. "govern everything with mercy" (PNEUMA). LOGOS's "ordering" preferred.

**v. 2** — "knowing your might" (EMET) vs. "knowing your power" (LOGOS) vs. "know your power" (PNEUMA). "power" for δύναμιν preferred (LOGOS/PNEUMA).

**v. 2** — "reckoned as yours" (EMET) vs. "counted as yours" (LOGOS) vs. "belong to you" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 3** — "perfect righteousness" (EMET) vs. "complete righteousness" (LOGOS) vs. "fullness of righteousness" (PNEUMA). Greek τελεία δικαιοσύνη = complete/full/perfect righteousness. LOGOS adopted.

**v. 4** — "evil device of men" (EMET, LOGOS) vs. "cunning scheme of men" (PNEUMA). PNEUMA interprets; EMET/LOGOS closer to πανουργία = craftiness/villainy. LOGOS/EMET preferred.

**v. 4** — "fruitless toil" (EMET) vs. "fruitless labor" (LOGOS) vs. "empty labour" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 4** — "a form besmeared with varied colors" (EMET) vs. "a form daubed with varied colors" (LOGOS) vs. "smeared over with a muddle of colours" (PNEUMA). "daubed" (LOGOS) preferred as precise and evocative.

**v. 5** — "entices fools into desire" (EMET) vs. "stirs fools to longing" (LOGOS) vs. "stirs up a fool's desire" (PNEUMA). LOGOS adopted.

**v. 5** — "breathless form of a dead image" (EMET) vs. "breathless form of a lifeless image" (LOGOS) vs. "lifeless shape of a painted image" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred; "lifeless" better than EMET's "dead" at the verse end. PNEUMA's "painted" is an addition.

**v. 6** — Word order: "those who make, desire, and worship such things" (EMET) vs. "those who make such things, who desire them, who worship them" (LOGOS) vs. "those who make such things, who want them, who bow down to them" (PNEUMA). LOGOS structure adopted; "worship" preferred over PNEUMA's "bow down."

**v. 7** — "for our service" (EMET) vs. "for our use" (LOGOS) vs. "for our daily use" (PNEUMA — adds "daily," not in text). LOGOS's "for our service" or "for our use" both work; SOPHIA: "for our service."

**v. 8** — "a vain god" (EMET) vs. "a god of no worth" (LOGOS) vs. "a worthless god" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 8** — "the debt of his soul is demanded back" (EMET) vs. "the debt of his soul is called in" (LOGOS) vs. "the debt of his life is called due" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 9** — "his concern is not that he will labor" (EMET) vs. "his concern is not that he will wear himself out" (LOGOS) vs. "none of that troubles him — not the strain of the work" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 10** — "his hope is cheaper than dirt" (EMET) vs. "his hope more worthless than earth" (LOGOS) vs. "worth less than dirt" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 11** — "the one who formed him" (EMET) vs. "his Maker" (LOGOS) vs. "the one who formed him" (EMET, PNEUMA). LOGOS's "his Maker" is an interpretive shorthand; EMET/PNEUMA closer to Greek πλάσαντα. SOPHIA: "his Maker" for concision, with EMET's form for the second clause.

**v. 11** — "breathed into him an active soul" (EMET, LOGOS) vs. "blew the breath of life through him" (PNEUMA). "active soul" is more precise to ψυχὴν ἐνεργοῦσαν. EMET/LOGOS adopted.

**v. 12** — "reckoned our life as a plaything" (EMET) vs. "regarded our life as mere play" (LOGOS) vs. "treats our whole existence as a children's game" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 12** — "bazaar for gain" (EMET) vs. "marketplace for gain" (LOGOS) vs. "market stall for making money" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 13** — "this man above all others knows that he is sinning" (EMET) vs. "above all others who err, this man knows that he sins" (LOGOS reordered) vs. "above all sinners, this man knows he is doing wrong" (PNEUMA). SOPHIA restructures following LOGOS.

**v. 14** — "more wretched than the soul of a child" (EMET) vs. "more wretched than the soul of an infant" (LOGOS) vs. "more pitiable than even a newborn child" (PNEUMA). Greek νηπίου = infant/young child. LOGOS preferred.

**v. 15** — Body-part list: minor variation. EMET: "fingers of hands for touching." LOGOS: "fingers for grasping." PNEUMA: "stretch out fingers to touch." LOGOS preferred.

**v. 19** — Final verse is textually uncertain. EMET: "the creatures have been missed and praised by God." LOGOS: "these creatures have been excluded from God's blessing and praise." PNEUMA: "creatures passed over by God's blessing and praise alike." SOPHIA: "passed over by God's blessing and praise" — combining LOGOS and PNEUMA for clarity.
